'Clovis I is traditionally said to have died on 27 November 511'; the partition 'created the new political units of the Kingdoms of Rheims, Orléans, Paris and Soissons' (Theuderic I, Chlodomer, Childebert I, Chlothar I). 25 December 800: Charlemagne is crowned emperor. 'Leo proclaimed Charlemagne 'emperor of the Romans' (Imperator Romanorum) and crowned him' at St Peter's. The kingdom becomes the Carolingian Empire: same state, same colour.

801: Barcelona falls. Barcelona fell to the Franks in 797, was retaken by Córdoba in 799 and was conquered in 801 after a seven-month siege (Louis the Pious page); Charlemagne page 'culminating in the 801 capture of Barcelona'. Cliopatria adds 24 Córdoba cells in 800 and 36 more in 806 on the south side of the Pyrenees (-2.1 to 2.4 E, 41.3-42.7 N).

region.text: Holstein, the land of the Nordalbingians

ledger.note: 804: Nordalbingia goes to the Obotrites. 'Charlemagne deported 10,000 of them to Neustria and gave their now vacant lands to the loyal king of the Obotrites.' 18 cells (Holstein); Cliopatria draws it in 806.

806: 79 cells of the Croatian coast (14.4-16.8 E, 43.7-45.4 N) enter the shape as Cliopatria's Duchy of Croatia row (741-925) is cut there. The Charlemagne page names only 'Istria and Veneto' in the Adriatic dispute; Croatia and Dalmatia are not on it.

814: 38 cells on the eastern edge (8.8-18.9 E, 46.0-54.5 N) go to Cliopatria's Great Moravia row (3 more to Nitra): the Slavic marches. Louis became sole ruler after Charlemagne died in 814; the pages give no Moravian event.
814: 13 northern cells go to Cliopatria's Scandinavian row; the Charlemagne page has the Danish king Gudfred murdered in 810 and a settlement in 811 ('Hemming later sued for peace').
825: 24 cells of Pamplona (and 15 of Sobrarbe) leave the Frankish shape. The Louis the Pious page has only an ambush at Roncevaux 'c. 812' while Louis dealt with Pamplona.

827: the Bulgars take the March of Pannonia. 'in 827 the Bulgarians attacked the Franks in the March of Pannonia and regained their lands.' 171 cells (15.3-19.6 E, 44.9-47.7 N), drawn by Cliopatria from 830.
840: 125 Pannonian cells come back from Cliopatria's Bulgarian row; no page opened shows a Frankish reconquest. Louis the Pious died on 20 June 840.
August 843: Aquitaine passes with West Francia. 'Pepin II was granted the Kingdom of Aquitaine, but only under the authority of Charles.'

region.text: all lands west of the Rhône

ledger.note: 10 August 843: Charles the Bald receives West Francia. 'Charles received all lands west of the Rhône, called West Francia.'

region.text: the central strip and the kingdom of Italy

ledger.note: 10 August 843: Lothair I receives Middle Francia. 'the Low Countries, the Rhineland west of the Rhine, Lorraine, Alsace, Burgundy, Provence' with Italy and 'the two imperial cities, Aachen and Rome'.

region.text: all lands east of the Rhine

ledger.note: 10 August 843: Louis the German receives East Francia. He was 'guaranteed the kingship of all lands to the east of the Rhine'.

region.text: the realm of Louis the Pious, divided in three at Verdun

ledger.note: 10 August 843: the Treaty of Verdun ends the one Frankish realm. 'the treaty ... agreed to on 10 August 843, ended the Carolingian civil war' that followed Louis the Pious's death in 840 and Lothair's defeat at Fontenoy in 841. Cliopatria keeps the unified row to 849 and starts the three kingdoms in 850.

wars.name: Frankish conquest of Burgundy
wars.outcome: The Franks lost at Vézeronce on 25 June 524 (Chlodomer killed), took Autun in 532 and ended the Burgundian kingdom in 534; it was divided among the three Frankish rulers.
wars.note: Francia dates 'Burgundes (534)'. The earlier Frankish attack of 500-501 (Dijon) is the burgundian-kingdom dossier's and Clovis I's page.

wars.name: Frankish conquest of Thuringia
wars.outcome: Thuringia was conquered by Theuderic and Chlothar with Theudebert I's help and incorporated in 532.
wars.note: The Chlothar I page has Hermanafrid offering Theuderic part of Thuringia in 531 and gives no year for the conquest; Francia gives 532.

wars.name: Saxon revolt of 555-556
wars.outcome: Chlothar I imposed an annual tribute in 555; the Saxons revolted again between 555 and 556; no border moved.

wars.name: Wars of Chlothar II against his nephews

zones.text: the land cut from Chlothar II's realm at Dormelles: Beauvais, Amiens and Rouen remained to him

wars.outcome: Dormelles 599: Chlothar II was reduced to Beauvais, Amiens and Rouen; a first attempt at reconquest failed in 604; Theudebert was crushed at Toul and Tolbiac in 612; the whole realm was delivered to Chlothar in 613.
wars.note: The page dates Dormelles to 599 (the frankish-burgundy dossier says 600, Cliopatria draws 602).

wars.name: Wendish war of Dagobert I
wars.outcome: Dagobert's Austrasian forces lost at Wogastisburg in 631; his Alemannic and Lombard allies repelled the Wends, who attacked again the next year; the Saxons offered help in return for ending their tribute of 500 cows. No border moved.

wars.name: Revolt of Radulf in Thuringia
wars.outcome: Thuringia leaves direct Frankish rule under Radulf.
wars.note: The page says only 'After Dagobert's death in 639' Radulf rebelled; 641 is Cliopatria's year.

wars.name: Neustrian-Austrasian wars and the Battle of Tertry
wars.outcome: Ebroin nearly united all the Franks and was assassinated in 681; at Tertry in 687 Pepin of Herstal defeated the king and his mayor and became mayor of Austrasia, Neustria and Burgundy.
wars.note: Internal to the drawn realm: no border moved. Theuderic III had been nominal king of all the Franks since 679.

wars.name: Frisian wars of Pepin of Herstal and Charles Martel

zones.text: West Frisia around Utrecht and Frisia beyond the Vlie

wars.outcome: Utrecht fell between 690 and 692; Charles seized West Frisia on Radbod's death in 719; he beat the Frisians on the Boarn in 734.

wars.name: Civil war after Pepin of Herstal
wars.outcome: Compiègne 26 September 715, Vinchy 21 March 717, Soissons 718 (Chilperic II and Odo of Aquitaine defeated); Charles Martel acclaimed mayor over Austrasia in 718; Chilperic II died in 721 and Charles appointed Theuderic IV.
wars.note: The kingdom-of-neustria dossier dates the end of Neustria to 724.

wars.name: Charles Martel's campaigns in Bavaria and Alamannia
wars.outcome: Fighting in Bavaria 720-723, again in 725 and 728 (Duke Hugbert 'submitted to Frankish suzerainty'); in 730 Charles marched against Lantfrid, Duke of Alemannia, who had also become independent.
wars.note: Alamannia joins the Frankish shape in 732 (Cliopatria); Bavaria stays outside until 788.

wars.name: Charles Martel's war with Aquitaine and the Umayyad invasion
wars.outcome: Charles attacked Aquitaine in 731; the Umayyad army was defeated at the Battle of Tours between Tours and Poitiers in 732. Aquitaine stays outside this state's drawn shape.

wars.name: Charles Martel's campaigns in Provence and Septimania
wars.outcome: Campaigning in Provence and Septimania in 737; the uprising of Maurontus in Provence was checked in 739; Charles reorganised Burgundy 732-735.

wars.name: Conquest of Septimania
wars.outcome: Pepin chased the Arabs and Berbers from Septimania and conquered Narbonne in 759.

wars.name: War of Aquitaine
wars.outcome: Pepin opened the war in 760, captured strongholds in 763, Toulouse and Bordeaux in 767; Waiofar was assassinated in 768 and Hunald's capture under Charlemagne ended 'ten years of war'.
wars.note: Opened in 760 (Pepin the Short page: 'In 760, after conquering the Roussillon ... and denouncing Waiofar's actions'), as the aquitaine dossier has it; corrected from 763 by the eu-07-b reviewer.

wars.name: Lombard campaign of Charlemagne
wars.outcome: Pavia besieged in late 773; Desiderius deposed and Charlemagne King of the Lombards in 774.

wars.name: Saxon Wars
wars.outcome: Eresburg 772; Saxony but for Nordalbingia taken 775; reconquest 779; Widukind's revolt 782-785 (Süntel, Verden, baptism 785); revolt 792-794; Engrian rising 796; Bornhöved 798; 10,000 deported and their land given to the Obotrites 804.
wars.note: The page gives no events for 773-774, 778, 799 and 800; the Cliopatria shapes put the Saxon cells in and out of this state in 775-777, 778, 779-781, 782, 783-784, 785-792, 793, 794-799.

wars.name: Basque and Spanish campaigns

zones.text: the Spanish March: Barcelona and the south side of the Pyrenees

wars.outcome: The Roncevaux ambush of 778; Barcelona fell in 797, was retaken in 799 and conquered in 801 after a seven-month siege.

wars.name: Deposition of Tassilo III of Bavaria
wars.outcome: 787 invasion; Tassilo deposed and sent to a monastery in 788; Bavaria absorbed.

wars.name: Avar Wars
wars.outcome: 791 invasion beaten back by a horse epidemic; 793 abandoned for the Saxon revolt; 796 Pippin of Italy's army destroyed the khagan's 'ring' and the khagan submitted: 'Pannonia seized by Francia'.
wars.note: Einhard dates the start of the war to 788.

wars.name: Danish war of Charlemagne
wars.outcome: Charlemagne sent an army to secure Frisia against Gudfred (810); Gudfred was murdered; a settlement with Hemming followed in 811. No border moved.

wars.name: Breton campaign of Louis the Pious
wars.outcome: Louis was returning from a campaign to Brittany in 818 when he heard of Ermengarde's death. The page gives nothing else.

wars.name: Frankish-Bulgarian war in Pannonia
wars.outcome: The Bulgarians attacked the Franks in the March of Pannonia and regained their lands.

wars.name: Revolts against Louis the Pious
wars.outcome: Pepin of Aquitaine marched on Paris and Louis was captured near Compiègne (830); Field of Lies 833; Louis restored on 1 March 834. No border moved.

wars.name: Carolingian civil war

zones.text: the whole realm, overlordship claimed by Lothair I

wars.outcome: Lothair I claimed overlordship after Louis's death in 840; Louis the German and Charles the Bald beat him at Fontenoy in 841 and swore the Oaths of Strasbourg in 842; the Treaty of Verdun was agreed on 10 August 843.
wars.note: The three armies became the three successor states; the belligerents are named by the kingdoms they founded. The Kingdom of the Franks is the arena.

certainty.note: Merovingian frontiers are approximate: the shapes are Cliopatria's and the pages give cities and peoples, not lines. The sub-kingdom partitions (511, 561, 639) have no territorial lines on the pages.
Carolingian marches (Spanish, Breton, Pannonian, Saxon, Danish) were frontier zones; the Pyrenean and Elbe frontiers are the firmest, the Avar and Slavic ones the softest.

Treaty of Verdun: 'all lands west of the Rhône' and 'all lands to the east of the Rhine' are river lines; the page gives no line for Middle Francia's western edge (Scheldt, Meuse, Saône are not named).

notes:
Written 2026-10-25 by the Phase B research agent for eu-07-b from the 14 Wikipedia pages in sources (all loaded; none failed). One state covers all 50 Cliopatria 'Kingdom of the Franks' shapes (462..849): the Frankish realm as one drawn state from 509 (Clovis I unites all Franks) to 10 August 843 (Verdun). The partition kingdoms (Austrasia, Neustria, Paris, Orleans, Reims, Soissons, Metz, Burgundy) are internal divisions of that realm except where Cliopatria or a sibling dossier carries a row of its own (frankish-burgundy, kingdom-of-neustria, aquitaine, saxons, magna-frisia, duchy-of-thuringia and the others named as counterparts in the ledger); the ledger books a split and a regain wherever a sibling row takes land out of this shape, so the shape and the sibling never cover the same cells.

Cliopatria rows to correct (all in keyframe_review): the 462, 490 and 500 shapes (a 28.6 k km2 outline around Cologne) are marked wrong and not used, because the state begins in 509 and the earlier Frankish realms are in the salian-franks and ripuarian-franks dossiers; the 510 shape gains one year at the front (509). Burgundy is subtracted from the 561-592 shapes (the frankish-burgundy sibling carries the Burgundian share from 561 and Chlothar II's loss and regain of it 599-613). The 599-601 and 613-616 spans take the 602 and 617 outlines. The 661 and 666 Frankish row is a 136 km2 sliver near the Vilaine and then Austrasia alone; the Aquitaine rows of 661 and 666 are really the whole Frankish realm (the 674 shape is used instead; the aquitaine owner should re-check those two rows). Neustria is wrongly separated 724-731 (put back). The 732-749 shapes swallow the whole Aquitanian duchy (843 cells) although no page opened makes Aquitaine Frankish before 768; the Aquitaine outline is subtracted and drawn by the aquitaine dossier, the extra Languedoc and Septimania cells of the 741 shape are booked as a 739 gain from the Umayyads (Charles Martel's campaigns in Provence and Septimania, 737-739). The 775 shape contains Papal Romagna cells (left as Cliopatria draws them, ledger 775 gain from papal-states at confidence 1). The Saxon swings of 778-804 are drawn year by year from the Saxon Wars page (Cliopatria has Saxony in the shape in 775-777 and 788-792 and from 800, and out in 778-787 and 793-799: summer 779, the revolt of 782, the submission of 785 and the revolt of 792-794 are put in their own keyframes). Cliopatria's 793 shape already holds the Avar land (415 cells) although the khagan submitted only in 796 (Avar Wars page): it is taken out for 793-795, and 121 Avar cells leave in 800 (page silent, confidence 1). The Obotrite cells (Holstein) leave in 804. The Bulgar cells in Pannonia leave in 827. The row runs to 849 although Verdun is 10 August 843: the 840 shape is narrowed to 840-843 and the three successor dossiers (west-franks, middle-franks, east-franks) start in 843.

Odd rows that belong to other owners: Cliopatria's 'Frisia Kingdom' row (612-717) is geometrically Swabia (Alamannia), not Frisia (eu-06 should re-label it; the ledger books it as the counterpart of 644 and 718). The merovingian-empire dossier's Provence-only leaf rows duplicate Provence, which this dossier carries from 536; that row can be merged here or dropped.

Mirror events other dossiers should carry (the reverse side of this ledger): salian-franks end 509 and ripuarian-franks end 509 (merge); burgundian-kingdom ends 534; ostrogothic-kingdom loses Provence 536 (this dossier follows the Chlothar I page; Cliopatria and the ostrogothic dossier say 540); frankish-burgundy split 561, loss 599 and 612 (Dormelles), gain 613, split 639, gain 661; duchy-of-thuringia 567 vassal_start to 633, loss 641 (Radulf), gain 724, and kingdom-of-thuringia ends 532; aquitaine loss 629, gain 632, contest 731-732 and 760-768, gain 768, vassal 781-843; magna-frisia gain 692, loss 718, gain 719, gain 734, gain 772; kingdom-of-neustria contest 717-724; kingdom-of-alamannia loss 724, contest 730-732, gain 732; bavarians gain 788; saxons vassal 555-556 and 738-772, contests and gains 772-794; avar-khaganate contest 791, loss 796; frisians gain 800; obotrites loss 804; umayyad-caliphate loss of Septimania 759; emirate-of-cordoba loss of Septimania 759, gains 778, 783, Barcelona 801; kingdom-of-italy gain 774; papal-states 775; duchy-of-spoleto 778; duchy-of-gascony 783; duchy-of-benevento vassal 786-793; first-bulgarian-empire 827 and 840; duchy-of-croatia 806; great-moravia 814; scandinavian-minor-kingdoms (Danes) 814; kingdom-of-pamplona 825.

Disagreements between pages and Cliopatria: the Thuringian conquest is 532 on the Francia page and 534 in Cliopatria; the cession of Provence is 536 (Chlothar I page) and 540 (Cliopatria and the ostrogothic dossier); the Dormelles defeat is 599 on the Chlothar II page, 600 in the frankish-burgundy dossier and 602 in Cliopatria; Chlothar II died 628 on the Francia page and 629 on the Chlothar II page; Clovis's union of the Franks is c. 509 on the Francia infobox (the text calls the date unknown).
